questiontext.text: How can the approximate age of a felled tree from a temperate region be determined?

generalfeedback.text: Each annual growth ring represents one year's seasonal cycle of early and late wood growth; counting them estimates the tree's age.

answer.text: By counting the concentric annual growth rings on the stump cross-section

feedback.text: Correct! Each annual growth ring represents one year's seasonal cycle of early and late wood growth; counting them estimates the tree's age.

answer.text: By measuring the thickness of the dry outer bark with a micrometer

feedback.text: Incorrect. Each annual growth ring represents one year's seasonal cycle of early and late wood growth; counting them estimates the tree's age.

answer.text: By weighing the central spongy pith on a scale

feedback.text: Incorrect. Each annual growth ring represents one year's seasonal cycle of early and late wood growth; counting them estimates the tree's age.

answer.text: By counting the number of leaves on its uppermost branches
